Tom —

Appreciate the clear note and the annotated PDF. I looked it over and looped in Laura (Legal) and Ben (Customer Ops) so we can triage the redlines quickly. Quick answers/positioning from a product + ops POV:

1) Training / feedback license: our baseline is that customer content and feedback is not used for model retraining without explicit opt-in. We can codify an opt-in clause in the order form and, for customers that opt-in, provide a more detailed telemetry/evidence package.

2) Output ownership / productization carveouts: we're open to carveouts for specific modules where customers provide templates that are otherwise proprietary; we typically negotiate a limited license back to us for service improvements, but can discuss exclusivity / title in narrow scopes.

3) Escrow / holdback for derivatives: not standard for us, but we can consider an escrow-like compromise (e.g., temporary training hold + mediation clause) for high-risk modules. Need legal to weigh in on feasibility and risk.

Proposed next steps (timeline):
- Today (Mon): Laura to send first-pass redline for MSA and Order Form.
- Tue: internal review + call with OpenClaims legal to walk clauses.
- Wed: Ben to assemble evidence package template (telemetry, retention, KMS + audit summary).

Tom / Markus —

Thanks — I reviewed the OpenClaims redlines and prepared a first-pass counterproposal below with suggested language and rationale. I pasted the proposed clause text inline for your convenience. Please note: this is a commercial compromise intended to move the deal forward while limiting long-term model governance risk.

1) Training / Feedback License (Order Form checkbox + clause)
Proposed text (Order Form checkbox + short clause):

"Customer Data and Customer Feedback" shall mean the data, prompts, completions, and feedback that Customer submits or otherwise provides to Redwood in connection with the Services. Redwood shall not use Customer Data or Customer Feedback to train or improve models used to serve third parties without Customer's prior written opt-in. If Customer opts-in, Redwood will: (a) apply agreed anonymization and minimization safeguards; (b) provide an evidence pack (audit summary, retention logs, KMS key IDs) on request; and (c) limit any production retraining to models listed in Schedule A.

Rationale: explicit opt-in preserves OpenClaims' control; the schedule mechanism lets us list model variants allowed for retraining.

2) Output Title / Productization Carveouts (MSA Exhibit)
Proposed text:

"Title to Outputs": Except for Outputs that are pre-negotiated as Productized Modules in Exhibit B, Customer retains title to any Output that contains Customer proprietary templates or marked confidential information. For Productized Modules (Exhibit B), Customer grants Redwood a nonexclusive, worldwide, royalty-free license to reproduce and display Outputs for the purpose of providing, testing, and improving the Services; any use of Outputs to train models for third-party offerings requires Customer opt-in as set forth above.

Rationale: this gives customers clarity on their protected templates while allowing Redwood to operate the service.

3) Temporary Training Hold / Escrow-lite
Proposed approach: include a 6-month training hold if OpenClaims notifies Redwood of a dispute over a Productized Module; hold limits retraining using the disputed module's data pending mediation. Alternatively, OpenClaims may request a limited escrow of extracted feature vectors for independent review (cost + logistics to be negotiated).

Operational asks for evidence package (Ben):
- Ben to produce a 1-pager describing telemetry collected per request, retention windows, and KMS integration summary.
- Ben to map fields we can redact/anonymize for opt-in datasets.

Next steps:
- Ben to produce the evidence_request_template.xlsx and share by EOD Tue.
- Markus / Tom: confirm Tue 10:30am PT for a redline walk.
- If OpenClaims is comfortable, Laura to prepare markups and a concise sideletter to capture the productization carveouts.

Tom / team —

Operational clarifications from the customer-ops side to help finalize Exhibit B and Schedule A:
- Telemetry: we capture request metadata (timestamp, request ID, model variant, token counts) and have configurable retention windows. We do not routinely store full customer prompts beyond the retention window; where customers need longer retention we can offer a contract option.
- Anonymization: we can provide a pipeline that strips PII and token-level identifiers before any opt-in retraining exports; will require 4-6 week runbook to validate.
- Evidence pack: sample items we can provide initially: retention logs (CSV), key rotation timestamps, SOC2 control mapping, sample sanitized logs.

I'll assemble a pragmatic evidence_request_template.xlsx and tag items that are automated vs. manual. Draft will be in the drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB-OpenClaims-MSA-redlines (see Related Links).
